# Example: Children

#### Course: JavaScript in Browser

## Example: Children

As we've discussed previously, instead of selecting elements one by one, it's better to select their parent directly.

Suppose in the code below, you had to update the price of the first item in our price list from $2.50 to $3.00 when the "Update First Item" button is clicked.

```html
1<div class="container">
2    <h1>Price List</h1>
3    <ul id="price-list">
4        <li class="item">Milk <span>$2.50</span></li>
5        <li class="item">Bread <span>$1.50</span></li>
6        <li class="item">Toothpaste <span>$3.00</span></li>
7    </ul>
8    <button id="update">Update First Item</button>
9</div>
```

```javascript
1const priceList = document.querySelector("#price-list");
2const update = document.querySelector("#update")
```

Look at the script.js file. We have currently selected the parent, #price-list element.

![children](data:image/png;base64,)

To modify the price of the first item, you'll need to access the child of the price list first.
